about: A long gun or carbine (an AR-pattern rifle or pistol, a bolt-action, a sniper rifle). What its dossier must hold before modelling and where reliable data is found. AR-pattern parts are standardised: the military drawings and the makers' parts lists agree, and every part has a common name (upper receiver, lower receiver, bolt carrier group, buffer tube, handguard, muzzle device).

closeups.what: the muzzle device: its slots, ports, length
the handguard: its slots (M-LOK / KeyMod / rail), their pitch and count
upper and lower receiver: ejection port, forward assist, magazine well, pins
safety selector, magazine release, bolt catch, charging handle
the stock or brace and the buffer tube
the pistol grip and its texture
the magazine: body, ribs, floor plate
iron sights or the optic rail

research: 1 the maker's own page for THIS model (primary): every published size, quoted (kit dossier fact ... --quote)
2 the maker's manual and parts list; for AR-pattern parts also the military technical manual (TM 9-1005-319-23&P: public domain, parts by number) — kit dossier part ... --quote
3 patents: the maker's patent list, kit refs patent <number> (design patents: orthographic views)
4 the maker's pictures: gallery, turntable, press kit (measure-only for a private asset)
5 the tells against its siblings (barrel length, handguard, muzzle device, stock or brace), each with a source
6 two or more reference models: kit library find / get / inspect -> kit dossier add --kind model --measure ...
7 close-ups of every hero feature (the close-up list): parts retailers' photos
8 the owner's own photos when the owner has the object: they count as primary
never: forum posts as facts; Wikidata's numbers as the model's; pages on machine host names (kit/knowledge/sources.json)
